LESSON: PHRASAL VERBS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.1: Phrasal Verbs
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Phrasal Verbs, part of Strand 3 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How are phrasal verbs different from other verbs? 2. Why is it important to learn meanings of phrasal verbs?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. recognise signs of phrasa verbs for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Phrasal Verbs in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. identify phrasal verbs formed from break, hang, run and turn in texts,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Phrasal Verbs in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. use the given phrasal verbs in sentences of their own,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Phrasal Verbs in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. value the importance of using phrasal verbs in spoken, signed and written communication. • In groups, learners are guided to watch a signed demonstration or video of vocabulary related to phrasal verbs and personal grooming. • In pairs, learners are guided to fingerspell and sign vocabulary related to phrasal verbs and personal grooming. • Individually, learner is guided to search from digital and print sources for phrasal verbs formed from break, hang, run and turn and compile them in a word list. • In groups, learners are guided to search for the meanings of the phrasal verbs identified from print or non-print dictionaries and make notes. • Individually, learner is guided to form phrasal verbs from the given verbs and use them to fill in tables and broken passages. 1. How are phrasal verbs different from other verbs? 2. Why is it important to learn meanings of phrasal verbs? 150 • Individually, learner is guided to sign the phrasal verbs. • Individually, learner is guided to use phrasal verbs to construct signed sentences based on personal grooming and health education and display the sentences in charts. • Individually, learner is guided to post the charts in class and take a gallery walk assessing and reviewing the sentences. • Individually, learner is guided to suggest examples of writing, speaking and signing in context situations in which the given phrasal verbs could be used. • In pairs, learners are guided to sign sing songs with phrasal verbs on personal grooming.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Phrasal Verbs in the Kenya CBC curriculum.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Phrasal Verbs together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Self-efficacy: the learner confidently gain competence in using phrasal verbs.
